Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of CBD vs DMSO, provide a discussion of the genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cells.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Cannabidiol (CBD) treatment versus DMSO control was profiled by RNA-seq in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines (CBD_IC50 vs DMSO; raw counts: ijms-24-14743-v2-cbd_vs_dmso_raw_counts.csv; metadata: ijms-24-14743-v2-cbd_vs_dmso_metadata.csv). Differential expression was analyzed by DESeq2 and followed by preranked GSEA (KEGG_2016, GO_Biological_Process_2023, Reactome_Pathways_2024, MSigDB_Hallmark_2020) and ORA (MSigDB_Hallmark_2020, KEGG_2021_Human). Key enriched themes included metabolic reprogramming, inflammatory/hypoxic responses, cell-cycle control, and apoptosis. For any detail not specified (e.g., exact cell-line identity, replicate numbers), “not specified” is stated.  

Keywords  
• Hypoxia  
• p53 signaling  
• Inflammation (TNF-α/NF-κB)  
• Metabolism (glycolysis/cholesterol)  
• Cell-cycle (E2F targets)  

Candidate Genes  
VEGFA, TP53, JUN, CDKN1A, HK2, SLC2A1  

Pathway Enrichments  
Using preranked GSEA, the fraction of positively versus negatively enriched terms per library was:  
• KEGG_2016: 4/10 up (40%), 6/10 down (60%), ratio 0.67  
• GO_Biological_Process_2023: 109/145 up (75%), 36/145 down (25%), ratio 3.03  
• Reactome_Pathways_2024: 41/70 up (59%), 29/70 down (41%), ratio 1.41  
• MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 7/9 up (78%), 2/9 down (22%), ratio 3.50

| Leukocyte transendothelial migration  | Up        | CLDN1, RAPGEF4, MYL2, CLDN6, MMP9, ICAM1, CXCR4, CLDN4 |

| Coagulation          | Down      | CTSO, SPARC, THBD, C3     |  

Analysis  
CBD treatment drives a pronounced up-regulation of hypoxia (78% of Hallmark terms), glycolysis (Hallmark), fatty acid uptake (KEGG_2016), and p53-mediated stress responses, indicating metabolic reprogramming coupled to a stress/hypoxic signature. TNF-α/NF-κB signaling and neutrophil-related chemotaxis processes are also strongly induced, suggesting an inflammatory component. Conversely, cell-cycle E2F targets are among the most strongly down-regulated modules (NES ≈ –3.05), consistent with CDKN1A (p21) activation and suppression of DNA replication licensing (MCM4/5, ORC6). Translation elongation and ribosomal biogenesis pathways are uniformly up-regulated at the Reactome level, pointing to selective control of protein synthesis machinery. Apoptotic hallmarks appear enriched but to a lesser extent, supporting a partial pro-apoptotic effect. Overall, CBD reprograms CRC cells toward a hypoxic/inflammatory, metabolically active yet cell-cycle-arrested state.  

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
ORA of significant DE genes filtered for “p53” yielded:  
| Gene_set             | Term                   | Adjusted P-value | Leading Genes (subset)         |  
|----------------------|------------------------|------------------|--------------------------------|  
| KEGG_2021_Human      | p53 signaling pathway  | 2.96 × 10⁻⁶      | CDKN1A, BAX, GADD45A, MDM2, TP53 |  
| MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 | p53 Pathway            | 6.41 × 10⁻¹⁰     | CDKN1A, JUN, APAF1, SFN, TP53  |  

Both KEGG and Hallmark p53 modules are highly enriched (FDR < 10⁻⁵), confirming activation of cell-cycle arrest and DNA damage responses (CDKN1A, BAX, MDM2, SFN).  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
Up  
| Gene      | Direction | Role/Function                          | Pathway(s)                         |  
|-----------|-----------|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|  
| VEGFA     | Up        | Angiogenic growth factor, hypoxia      | Hypoxia; TNF-α signaling           |  
| TP53      | Up        | Tumor suppressor, DNA damage response | p53 Pathway; Apoptosis             |  
| JUN       | Up        | AP-1 transcription factor, stress      | TNF-α signaling; MAPK signaling    |  
| CDKN1A    | Up        | CDK inhibitor p21, cell-cycle arrest   | p53 Pathway; E2F Targets           |  
| HK2       | Up        | Hexokinase 2, glycolytic control       | Glycolysis                         |  
| SLC2A1    | Up        | Glucose transporter GLUT1              | Glycolysis; Hypoxia                |  

Down  
| Gene      | Direction | Role/Function                          | Pathway(s)                         |  
|-----------|-----------|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------|  
| MCM4      | Down      | DNA replication licensing factor       | E2F Targets                        |  
| MCM5      | Down      | DNA replication licensing factor       | E2F Targets                        |  
| ORC6      | Down      | Origin Recognition Complex component   | E2F Targets                        |  
| UBE2S     | Down      | Ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme           | E2F Targets                        |  

Comparisons  
The pattern of hypoxic/metabolic and inflammatory induction cooperates with p53-driven cell-cycle arrest, a profile distinct from typical proliferative CRC signatures. E2F-target down-regulation is a consistent feature across contrasts, whereas translation elongation up-regulation may reflect selective mRNA translation of stress-response transcripts.  

Implications  
These data suggest CBD reprograms CRC cells into a metabolically stressed, hypoxia-like state coupled to cell-cycle inhibition and pro-inflammatory signaling, which may sensitize cells to apoptosis or render them more vulnerable to combination with DNA-damage or metabolic inhibitors.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate up-regulation of HK2/SLC2A1 and glycolytic flux changes (e.g., lactate assays).  
2. Confirm p53 pathway activation by measuring p21 (CDKN1A) and MDM2 protein levels.  
3. Assess replication stress via EdU incorporation and γH2AX foci (H2AX) assays.  
4. Examine mitochondrial function and ROS production to probe translation elongation and oxidative stress modules.
